11: # Algebraic quotients
12: 
13: This file defines notation for algebraic quotients, e.g. quotient groups `G ⧸ H`,
14: quotient modules `M ⧸ N` and ideal quotients `R ⧸ I`.
15: 
16: The actual quotient structures are defined in the following files:
17: * Quotient Group: `Mathlib/GroupTheory/QuotientGroup/Defs.lean`
18: * Quotient Module: `Mathlib/LinearAlgebra/Quotient/Defs.lean`
19: * Quotient Ring: `Mathlib/RingTheory/Ideal/Quotient/Defs.lean`
20: 
21: ## Notation
22: 
23: The following notation is introduced:
24: 
25: * `G ⧸ H` stands for the quotient of the type `G` by some term `H`
26:   (for example, `H` can be a normal subgroup of `G`).
27:   To implement this notation for other quotients, you should provide a `HasQuotient` instance.
28:   Note that since `G` can usually be inferred from `H`, `_ ⧸ H` can also be used,
29:   but this is less readable.
30: 
31: ## Tags
32: 
33: quotient, group quotient, quotient group, module quotient, quotient module, ring quotient,
34: ideal quotient, quotient ring
35: -/
36: 
37: public section
38: 
39: 
40: universe u v
41: 
42: /-- `HasQuotient A B` is a notation typeclass that allows us to write `A ⧸ b` for `b : B`.
43: This allows the usual notation for quotients of algebraic structures,
44: such as groups, modules and rings.
45: 
46: `A` is a parameter, despite being unused in the definition below, so it appears in the notation.
47: -/
48: class HasQuotient (A : outParam <| Type u) (B : Type v) where
49:   /-- `HasQuotient.Quotient A b` (denoted as `A ⧸ b`) is the quotient of the type `A` by `b`. -/
50:   Quotient (A) : B → Type max u v
51: 
52: /-- A deprecated variant of `HasQuotient.Quotient` -/
53: @[deprecated HasQuotient.Quotient (since := "2025-12-18")]
54: abbrev HasQuotient.quotient' {A : outParam <| Type u} {B : Type v}
55:     [HasQuotient A B] (b : B) : Type max u v :=
56:   HasQuotient.Quotient A b
57: 
58: /-- Quotient notation based on the `HasQuotient` typeclass -/
59: notation:35 G " ⧸ " H:34 => HasQuotient.Quotient G H

12: /-!
13: # The `ZMod n`-module structure on Abelian groups whose elements have order dividing `n`
14: -/
15: 
16: @[expose] public section
17: 
18: assert_not_exists TwoSidedIdeal
19: 
20: variable {n : ℕ} {M M₁ : Type*}
21: 
22: /-- The `ZMod n`-module structure on commutative monoids whose elements have order dividing `n ≠ 0`.
23: Also implies a group structure via `Module.addCommMonoidToAddCommGroup`.
24: See note [reducible non-instances]. -/
25: abbrev AddCommMonoid.zmodModule [NeZero n] [AddCommMonoid M] (h : ∀ (x : M), n • x = 0) :
26:     Module (ZMod n) M := by
27:   have h_mod (c : ℕ) (x : M) : (c % n) • x = c • x := by
28:     suffices (c % n + c / n * n) • x = c • x by rwa [add_nsmul, mul_nsmul, h, add_zero] at this
29:     rw [Nat.mod_add_div']
30:   have := NeZero.ne n
31:   match n with
32:   | n + 1 => exact {
33:     smul := fun (c : Fin _) x ↦ c.val • x
34:     smul_zero := fun _ ↦ nsmul_zero _
35:     zero_smul := fun _ ↦ zero_nsmul _
36:     smul_add := fun _ _ _ ↦ nsmul_add _ _ _
37:     one_smul := fun _ ↦ (h_mod _ _).trans <| one_nsmul _
38:     add_smul := fun _ _ _ ↦ (h_mod _ _).trans <| add_nsmul _ _ _
39:     mul_smul := fun _ _ _ ↦ (h_mod _ _).trans <| mul_nsmul' _ _ _
40:   }
41: 
42: /-- The `ZMod n`-module structure on Abelian groups whose elements have order dividing `n`.
43: See note [reducible non-instances]. -/
44: abbrev AddCommGroup.zmodModule {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] (h : ∀ (x : G), n • x = 0) :
45:     Module (ZMod n) G :=
46:   match n with
47:   | 0 => AddCommGroup.toIntModule G
48:   | _ + 1 => AddCommMonoid.zmodModule h
49: 
50: /-- The quotient of an abelian group by a subgroup containing all multiples of `n` is a
51: `n`-torsion group. -/
52: -- See note [reducible non-instances]
53: abbrev QuotientAddGroup.zmodModule {G : Type*} [AddCommGroup G] {H : AddSubgroup G}
54:     (hH : ∀ x, n • x ∈ H) : Module (ZMod n) (G ⧸ H) :=
55:   AddCommGroup.zmodModule <| by simpa [QuotientAddGroup.forall_mk, ← QuotientAddGroup.mk_nsmul]
56: 
57: variable {F S : Type*} [AddCommGroup M] [AddCommGroup M₁] [FunLike F M M₁]
58:   [AddMonoidHomClass F M M₁] [Module (ZMod n) M] [Module (ZMod n) M₁] [SetLike S M]
59:   [AddSubgroupClass S M] {x : M} {K : S}

61: namespace ZMod

63: theorem map_smul (f : F) (c : ZMod n) (x : M) : f (c • x) = c • f x := by
64:   rw [← ZMod.intCast_zmod_cast c]
65:   exact map_intCast_smul f _ _ (cast c) x
66: 
67: theorem smul_mem (hx : x ∈ K) (c : ZMod n) : c • x ∈ K := by
68:   rw [← ZMod.intCast_zmod_cast c, Int.cast_smul_eq_zsmul]
69:   exact zsmul_mem hx (cast c)
70: 
71: end ZMod
72: 
73: variable (n)
74: 
75: namespace AddMonoidHom
76: 
77: /-- Reinterpret an additive homomorphism as a `ℤ/nℤ`-linear map.
78: 
79: See also:
80: `AddMonoidHom.toIntLinearMap`, `AddMonoidHom.toNatLinearMap`, `AddMonoidHom.toRatLinearMap` -/
81: def toZModLinearMap (f : M →+ M₁) : M →ₗ[ZMod n] M₁ := { f with map_smul' := ZMod.map_smul f }
82: 
83: theorem toZModLinearMap_injective : Function.Injective <| toZModLinearMap n (M := M) (M₁ := M₁) :=
84:   fun _ _ h ↦ ext fun x ↦ congr($h x)
85: 
86: @[simp]
87: theorem coe_toZModLinearMap (f : M →+ M₁) : ⇑(f.toZModLinearMap n) = f := rfl

arguments.statement: ∀ (sigma : LR.R p →+* ZMod p), Function.Surjective sigma → RingHom.ker sigma = Ideal.span {(p : LR.R p)} → ∃ s : Module (ZMod p) (LR.QMR p M), letI := s; ∀ (r : LR.R p) (z : LR.QMR p M), r • z = sigma r • z
arguments.proof:
intro sigma hs hk
classical
let Q := LR.QMR p M
let phi : LR.R p →+* AddMonoid.End Q := Module.toAddMonoidEnd _ _
have hp : phi (p : LR.R p) = 0 := by
  ext z
  obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := (LR.pMR p M).mkQ_surjective z
  change (LR.pMR p M).mkQ ((p : LR.R p) • m) = 0
  apply (Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero _).2
  exact ⟨m, rfl⟩
have hkphi : RingHom.ker sigma ≤ RingHom.ker phi := by
  rw [hk]
  exact Ideal.span_le.2 (by simpa only [Set.singleton_subset_iff, RingHom.mem_ker] using hp)
let psi := sigma.liftOfSurjective hs ⟨phi, hkphi⟩
letI s : Module (ZMod p) Q := Module.compHom Q psi
refine ⟨s, ?_⟩
intro r z
change phi r z = psi (sigma r) z
rw [RingHom.liftOfSurjective_comp_apply]

arguments.statement: ∀ (sigma : LR.R p →+* ZMod p), Function.Surjective sigma → RingHom.ker sigma = Ideal.span {(p : LR.R p)} → ∃ s : Module (ZMod p) (LR.QMR p M), letI := s; ∀ (r : LR.R p) (z : LR.QMR p M), r • z = sigma r • z
arguments.proof:
intro sigma hs hk
classical
let Q := LR.QMR p M
let phi : LR.R p →+* AddMonoid.End Q := Module.toAddMonoidEnd _ _
have hp : phi (p : LR.R p) = 0 := by
  ext z
  obtain ⟨m, rfl⟩ := (LR.pMR p M).mkQ_surjective z
  change (LR.pMR p M).mkQ ((p : LR.R p) • m) = 0
  apply (Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero _).2
  exact ⟨m, rfl⟩
have hkphi : RingHom.ker sigma ≤ RingHom.ker phi := by
  rw [hk]
  apply Ideal.span_le.2
  intro a ha
  have ha' : a = (p : LR.R p) := Set.mem_singleton_iff.1 ha
  subst a
  exact (RingHom.mem_ker).2 hp
let psi := sigma.liftOfSurjective hs ⟨phi, hkphi⟩
letI s : Module (ZMod p) Q := Module.compHom Q psi
refine ⟨s, ?_⟩
intro r z
change phi r z = psi (sigma r) z
rw [RingHom.liftOfSurjective_comp_apply]

letI := c
letI := rho.toAlgebra
letI := ZMod.algebra K p
letI := s
intro ha
have hs := hr.2.2.1
have hfac := hr.2.2.2.2.2
have hrK (r : LR.R p) (k : K) : r • k = sigma r • k := by
  change rho r * k = algebraMap (ZMod p) K (sigma r) * k
  rw [hfac]

letI : TensorProduct.CompatibleSMul (ZMod p) (LR.R p) K (LR.QMR p M) := ⟨by

  intro t k z

  rw [← hrK, ← ha]

  rw [← hu]
  change TensorProduct.tmul (LR.R p) k ((p : LR.R p) • u) = 0
  rw [← TensorProduct.smul_tmul]
  have hpk : (p : LR.R p) • k = (0 : K) := by
    simp [Algebra.smul_def, CharP.cast_eq_zero K p]
  rw [hpk, TensorProduct.zero_tmul]
let q := TensorProduct.AlgebraTensorModule.tensorQuotientEquiv K (LR.R p) K (LR.pMR p M)
let e0 := (q.trans (Submodule.quotEquivOfEqBot _ hz)).symm
let e1 := TensorProduct.equivOfCompatibleSMul (ZMod p) (LR.R p) K K (LR.QMR p M)
refine ⟨e0.trans e1, ?_⟩
intro k m
have he0 : e0 (TensorProduct.tmul (LR.R p) k m) = TensorProduct.tmul (LR.R p) k ((LR.pMR p M).mkQ m) := by
  apply e0.symm.injective
  simp [e0, q]
simpa [he0]
